\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Definitions}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.Definitions
\section{Overview}
The stable and noisy cubes are weighted directed graphs whose edge weights record correlated uniform-bit pairs. Loops are retained, and their weights are defined for every real noise parameter.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Weighted directed graph]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
\leanok
A weighted directed graph on a set $V$ consists of a directed graph on $V$, with loops permitted, together with a real weight $w(x,y)$ for every ordered pair $x,y\in V$; no positivity or support condition is imposed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Joint-law weights of a stable cube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.stableCubeGraph}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and $\rho\in\bbr$, the $\rho$-stable cube is the complete directed graph, including loops, on $\{0,1\}^n$, with weight $w(x,y)=2^{-n}\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{1+\rho(-1)^{x_i+y_i}}{2}$. For $-1\le\rho\le1$, these weights are the joint probabilities of a uniform correlated pair.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bit-flip probability as a weighted graph]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noisyCubeGraph}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.stableCubeGraph}
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and $\delta\in\bbr$, the $\delta$-noisy cube is the $(1-2\delta)$-stable cube: the complete directed graph on $\{0,1\}^n$ with weights $2^{-n}\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{1+(1-2\delta)(-1)^{x_i+y_i}}{2}$.
\end{definition}
